paperTitle: Database Management Systems - End Semester Examination
courseOutcomes: CO1: Explain database concepts, architecture, and data models
CO2: Design relational schemas using keys and constraints
CO3: Write SQL queries for data definition and manipulation
CO4: Analyze normalization and transaction management
instructions: Write SQL queries using standard SQL syntax

questions.text: Explain the three-schema architecture of a database management system.
Explain primary key, candidate key, foreign key, and referential integrity with examples.

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: Write an SQL query to display the names of students who scored more than 80 marks.

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: Write an SQL query to find the average marks for each course.

orOptions.label: A
orOptions.text: Explain the process of converting an ER diagram into relational tables.

orOptions.label: B
orOptions.text: Explain functional dependency and normalize a relation up to Third Normal Form.

orOptions.label: A
orOptions.text: Explain transaction states and the ACID properties of transactions.

orOptions.label: B
orOptions.text: Describe two-phase locking and explain how it prevents concurrency problems.

questions.text: Design a relational database for a library system and list suitable tables, attributes, keys, and relationships.
